description:
=== DONE (s470bu) ===

THE COST.  `do-regex-subst` rebuilt the whole pattern pipeline on EVERY
evaluation of every s///:

  * `perl-regex-to-ppcre` on the pattern text â SIX `cl-ppcre:regex-replace-all`
    passes over it;
  * `perl-to-ppcre-replacement` on the replacement;
  * seven `member` walks of the modifier list (:e :g :r :i :s :m :x);
  * an `append`ed options list;
  * `%pcl-create-scanner`, whose cache key is FORMATted out of the whole
    pattern plus the options.

`sb-sprof` over the `json-rt` macro row (26 973 samples, s470bn's instrument):
`perl-regex-to-ppcre` alone was **33.1 %** of the run, reached from
`do-regex-subst` (json-graph.txt line 116).  m// has had a compiled slot since
task #680; s/// never got one.

THE FIX.  `%p-subst-compiled` builds the record

    #(pattern replacement scanner eval-p global-p non-destructive-p
      reg-names closers)

ONCE and keeps it in the op.  The record is a pure function of the op's three
data slots (pattern / replacement / modifiers) and nothing writes those after
the op is built, so THE OP IS THE CACHE â there is no invalidation rule to get
wrong.  `do-regex-subst` reads the eight fields and does nothing else that the
pattern text can reach.

THE SLOT HOLDS A CONS, not the record.  That is the whole reason the lever is
worth more than a rename: an s/// whose replacement is a CLOSURE must build a
FRESH op per evaluation (the closure may capture lexicals â that is #1250's
own negative), and a cache that lives in a per-evaluation op caches nothing.
Because the record does NOT depend on the closure (a `functionp` replacement
is always eval-p, so it has no translated replacement of its own), the CONS
can be a per-SITE cell: `%p-op-site` (task #1250's `(load-time-value (cons nil
nil) nil)`, now named) is passed to `%p-subst-parts` whenever the `p-subst`
macro proved the PATTERN and FLAGS constant.  That is every interpolated
replacement and every s///e â JSON::PP's hot ones included.  A run-time
pattern gets a private cons and behaves exactly as before.

WHERE THE RECORD IS BUILT.  Inside `do-regex-subst`'s `handler-case`, so a bad
pattern still warns and answers 0 exactly where it did when the scanner was
built per call; and the record is stored only on success, so a retry
re-signals rather than caching a half-built one.  The defstruct slot defaults
to a fresh cons so an op built by `make-p-subst-op` directly still has a holder
(a nil there would die in `(setf (car nil) â¦)`).

MEASURED.  `tools/bench-exec.pl` with `BENCH_RT_B=<main's runtime>` â one
transpile, two cores, INTERLEAVED best-of-5, startup subtracted (A = this
branch, B = main 31473881; load average 5.4 at start, 4.7 at end â a sibling
agent was running a CPAN dist suite, so the control rows are the honest
spread):

  bench        perl(s)   pclA(s)   pclB(s)      B/A    A/perl
  json-rt       1.2436    2.2246    4.4768  +101.2%     1.79x   <- the profiled row, HALVED
  subste        0.0747    0.3462    0.5876   +69.7%     4.63x
  regexg        0.5056    1.0354    1.2999   +25.6%     2.05x   (that one is #1250)
  textproc      0.5919    2.6250    2.9405   +12.0%     4.43x
  intloop+=     0.0874    0.0280    0.0278    -0.9%     0.32x   control
  sortstr       0.0921    0.1476    0.1489    +0.8%     1.60x   control
  moo-objs      0.0400    2.0819    2.1000    +0.9%    51.99x   control
  strcat        0.4033    0.8547    0.8907    +4.2%     2.12x   control (spread)

json-rt goes 3.60x perl -> **1.79x perl**.  Isolating #1251 from #1250
(`scratch/s470bu/ab-rt.pl`, one program two runtimes, best-of-5, B = this
branch's own HEAD~1 = #1250 only):

  subste  0.6283 -> 0.3550  **-43.5 %**
  substg  0.4526 -> 0.4280  -5.4 %   (s/// on a LONG subject: the per-call cost
                                      is amortised over the scan, which is why
                                      `subste` â many s/// on SHORT subjects,
                                      the shape CPAN code has â is the row this
                                      lever is felt on and was added to
                                      `tools/bench-exec.pl`)

Well above the round's 20 %-of-its-row bar.

BARS.  Guard `Pl/t/perf-levers-03.t` 11 -> 18 rows: the record is absent on a
fresh op, built once, and the SAME object comes back; it carries the
TRANSLATED pattern (`[[:digit:]]` -> `[0-9]` â cl-ppcre does not know the POSIX
class, so seeing `[0-9]` proves the translation happened and was KEPT); the
site appears for a constant pattern behind a closure replacement and NOT for a
run-time pattern; a closure replacement has no translated replacement; and a
19-shape RUN row against perl 5.40.3 (the /x /i /m /s /g /r modifiers, a
translated POSIX class and \x{}, \Q..\E, a named capture in the replacement, a
backreference, the count/"" dualvar, one op on two different subjects, a
run-time pattern at a site that must not cache, tr///cs).  INVERSE-verified on
a `git archive 31473881` extraction: rows 1/2/5/7/10/12/13/14/15 fail there,
the six NEGATIVES and the three RUN rows pass â which is the design (the RUN
rows assert semantics the lever must not change).

RUNTIME-ONLY.  `%p-op-site` is inserted by the runtime's own macro and is never
named in emitted text, so `pl2cl`'s output is unchanged: `tools/corpus-diff.pl
31473881` IDENTICAL across 111 files (silent drops 5, unchanged),
`tools/emission-ab.pl --shapes --list lib/**/*.pm` 27/27 SAME 0 DIFF 0 RCDIFF.
No `PCL_OPT` name (it is not a licensed emission), no generation bump, no
artifact regeneration â the #1181 / #1203-#1205 precedent.
subject: perf: the s/// op carries its COMPILED record (%p-subst-compiled) â m//'s #680 for substitution
